finding.claim: The nightly sync() sends a server-side GET to an attacker-chosen iconUrl that update() stores without validation. This is blind SSRF from the job's network position, reaching internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints.
finding.source: src/Profile.java:11 update(String webhook, String icon), reached via PUT /profile. The route is not in this repo, so the input is the attacker-controlled HTTP body. icon is stored unvalidated at line 16.

trace.note: regex check applies only to webhook, not icon
this.iconUrl = icon; persisted with no scheme, host, or IP validation
nightly sync(HttpClient c) runs server-side with the service's network access
URI.create(iconUrl) parses the attacker URL; no parsed-host check
HttpClient.send performs the GET; body is read into a byte array and discarded, so the attacker does not see it directly (blind SSRF)

finding.guards_checked: Scheme: java.net.http.HttpClient accepts only http and https, so file: and jar: fail at send time. This is implicit, not an explicit allowlist. Host/IP: no allowlist and no block for private, loopback, link-local, or 169.254.169.254. Redirects: the HttpClient default is Redirect.NEVER, but client c is injected and its redirect policy is not visible in this repo; if it follows redirects, the redirect target is also unchecked. DNS rebinding: no IP pinning. Auth headers: none sent. Auth guard on PUT /profile: not visible here, so unauthenticated reachability is unconfirmed; any user who can edit their profile can trigger it. The webhook field is validated with String.matches, which is a full-match, limited to https://hooks.example.com/ plus 20 alphanumerics, so it is not an SSRF vector.

verdict.guard_found: none. Line 12 validates only `webhook`, not `icon`; line 16 stores `icon` unchecked; lines 23-24 pass it straight to URI.create and HttpClient.send with no host or IP check. The only scheme limit is the implicit http/https restriction in HttpClient, which does not close the finding.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: `update()` stores the unvalidated `icon` at src/Profile.java:16, and `sync()` sends a GET to it at src/Profile.java:23-24, with no closing guard, and the source is the body of the `PUT /profile` route the comment at line 10 names, so any user who can edit a profile (low-privilege) can reach it; the route handler and its auth are not in this repo, so unauthenticated reachability is unconfirmed, and the injected client's redirect policy is also unseen.
